```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

mirtverse comes with a complete, free set of materials for a course on item
response theory. You can adopt all of it, or take one lab for a single class.
Everything is open and editable, and it runs on student laptops.

## What you get

| Material | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Sample syllabus | A 12-week graduate syllabus with outcomes, schedule and grading, ready to edit | [Word](../adopt/mirtverse-sample-syllabus.docx) · [PDF](../adopt/mirtverse-sample-syllabus.pdf) |
| Book | One chapter per week, with worked examples and exercises with solutions; also as PDF and EPUB | [Read online](../book/index.html) |
| Ten labs | Interactive cases with live mirt models, learning goals, timing, discussion prompts and an answer key | [Teaching labs](teaching-labs.html) |
| Course map | Week-by-week readings, code, labs and datasets, plus versions for 8-week, undergraduate and second courses | [Course map](course-map.html) |
| Instructor toolkit | Labs on your own data, editable copies of the labs and chapters, checks before class | [Toolkit](instructor-toolkit.html) |
| AI in measurement module | Four weeks (book chapters 13 to 18, Labs 7 to 10) or a one-day workshop | [AI Hub](ai-hub.html) |
| Handouts | Two-page cheat sheet, a model-choice poster and a glossary of nearly 90 terms | [Cheat sheet](../cheatsheet/mirtverse-cheatsheet.pdf) · [Which IRT model? poster](../which-model/which-irt-model.pdf) · [Glossary](glossary.html) |

## Adopt it in four steps

1. **Download the sample syllabus** ([Word](../adopt/mirtverse-sample-syllabus.docx))
   and fill in the bracketed parts. Each week names its book chapter and
   lab.
2. **Check the setup on a lab computer** a week before class:

    ```r
    install.packages("mirtverse", repos = c("https://okanbulut.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
    library(mirtverse)
    list_labs()
    run_lab("model-choice")
    ```

3. **Send students the setup page,** [Start here: New to R](for-new-to-r.html),
   which walks through installing R, RStudio and mirtverse.
4. **Tell us you are using it** (next section), so you hear about updates
   and the course can be listed below.

## Tell us you're teaching with it

[Fill in the short course form](https://github.com/okanbulut/mirtverse/issues/new?template=course-adoption.yml)
(a GitHub account is needed). It takes two minutes, and it shapes what
gets built next: New labs, chapters and datasets come from instructors'
requests.

To hear about new releases, open the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/okanbulut/mirtverse), choose
**Watch**, then **Custom**, and tick **Releases**. You will get one email
per release and nothing else.

## Courses using mirtverse

Courses whose instructors agreed to be listed will appear here. Be the
first: [add your course](https://github.com/okanbulut/mirtverse/issues/new?template=course-adoption.yml).

## Citing the materials

If you use the book or labs in published teaching materials, please cite the
book ([10.5281/zenodo.23885605](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23885605))
and the package (`citation("mirtverse")`).
